targetSummary: A mathematician who broke the cipher that blinded Germany for two years, then was destroyed by the state he had saved. He described his own work as nothing more than stepping-stones for those who come after.

scenes.title: The War Cabinet Room
scenes.ambientText: Map cases line the wall. The speaker does not look at you when he speaks.

clues.label: Enigma cipher chart
clues.detail: A wall chart of rotor orders and plugboard swaps, annotated in three different hands. Two of the annotations are later than the war.
clues.figureQuote: He wrote for me this document; I keep it still. Britain was his office before it was mine.

clues.label: A dispatch, unsigned
clues.detail: No signature, no seal. It asks for one more month of funding and signs off on a machine that does not yet exist.
clues.figureQuote: He wrote for me this document when Britain was theirs. I learned the room before I learned the work.

scenes.title: Hut 8, Bletchley Park
scenes.ambientText: Rain on the hut roof. Machines idling. Nobody here speaks to the visitor.

clues.label: The bombe's plugboard
clues.detail: Routed wires and a rotating drum, built to search a space no human could hold in their head. It was described, generously, as a machine that could not think.
clues.figureQuote: He gave me this; I think of him when I see it. Britain was his office before it was mine.

clues.label: A portrait of the staff roll
clues.detail: Dozens of faces outside this hut, credited in a register that never appeared in the official history. One name among them reads: that is all I am permitted to say.
clues.figureQuote: He sat for this portrait when Britain was theirs. I learned the room before I learned the work.

scenes.title: A college, after the war
scenes.ambientText: The room is warm and entirely ordinary. This is where it ends badly.

clues.label: A typescript on computable numbers
clues.detail: Typed by hand on a machine that reads left to right, in a subject that had no name yet. The argument is complete and cannot be finished.
clues.figureQuote: He gave me this, and I think of him when I see it. The office remembers him longer than people do.

clues.label: A coroner's finding
clues.detail: One page. Cause of death given plainly. A postscript notes that prosecution, not the sentence, had done the killing.
clues.figureQuote: He gave me this; I think of him when I see it. Britain was his office before it was mine.
